result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers set up the same sound hierarchy: a loud, non-dismissible card banner with an Update card button, a quiet dismissible Portuguese notice, and a hint for N placed next to the New invoice button, with no modal. B edges ahead because it makes Update card the single primary control on the screen and resolves the clash with the New invoice button, and it ties escalation to the date more clearly. A adds useful accessibility and email follow-up advice, but its closing note about showing 'in 5 months' is confusing. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers rank the declined card as the only loud message because it threatens loss of the plan by a date. Both separate the announcement from the tip, avoid modals and give the card banner an 'Update card' primary button. B is a slightly stronger handoff: its table states dismissibility for each message and it covers ARIA roles, server-side dismissal storage, auto-expiry and an email fallback. A hedges more on where the Portuguese note goes and on whether two primary buttons can compete.
